correctness_confidence.basis: Necessity chain checked: polar form (2) by hand; Lemma 2 angular identity numerically on a 2-factor example (agreement about 1e-8); f_c with zeta=(c+i)/s gives f'(0)=2ic/s and F+HG=c to 1e-12; min over c of (a+c)sqrt(1+c^2)/c equals (1+a^(2/3))^(3/2) for a=0.1 to 8. Lemma 3 identities not checkable from the text layer. Eq. (14) inconsistent as printed.

rigor.basis: Necessity via harmonic pairing is short and complete given Lemma 2. Sufficiency relies on an asserted eps->1 limit at the pole of M_c, on Lemma 3, and on Poisson and quantile steps. Proposition 4's displayed error term (4/N^2) does not follow from the stated argument, which gives O(1/N). Equality exclusion is justified by an unnecessary hypothesis.

novelty.basis: Exact threshold |b|^(2/3) < 1+a^(2/3) for weak, strict and local analytic certificates of the Liu-Fitzsimmons family. Prior work gives nonexistence only for |b| >= 2(a+1). Priority is self-reported. A web search found arXiv:2607.16171, but its snippet shows a different cubic field, so the family attribution is unverified by me.

significance.basis: Sharpens the certificate region of one planar cubic family and extends the threshold to odd-degree single harmonics (Corollary 6). Stability is not changed, since GAS is already known. No general converse theorem and no minimum-degree rate are given, so the scope is narrow but the result is clean.

reproducibility.basis: Analytic constructions are explicit, but the quantile selection and rigorous enclosures are not supplied. The floating-point diagnostic (2048 factors, 8192 samples, margin about 0.1545) and the Toeplitz solver runs come with no code or data. I did not run any author computation.

summary: Claims the exact certificate threshold for the cubic family (1): |b|^(2/3) < 1 + a^(2/3) for positive homogeneous polynomial weak certificates, strict product-of-quadratics certificates and local analytic certificates, with equality excluded. Necessity is a clean harmonic pairing argument (Lemma 2 factorization, test function f_c, minimization over c). I checked its key steps by hand and numerically. Sufficiency uses a boundary pair (Lemma 3), Poisson smoothing and quantile approximation to build a finite product of positive quadratic forms. I could not verify Lemma 3's explicit q_c and h_c from the text layer, and the eps->1 limit is asserted rather than written out. Eq. (14), as extracted (c = b^(2/3)-1), is inconsistent with a0 = c^3 and b0 = s^3 unless c = (b^(2/3)-1)^(1/2). The displayed error chain of Proposition 4 does not match its stated argument, which gives O(1/N); the existence claim does not depend on that constant. The local analytic and single-harmonic extensions follow the same template. The global stability claims rest on the Lyapunov function H, which I checked. Priority is self-reported and I could not confirm it. Verdict: plausible and substantive, but it needs corrections and a complete write-up of the boundary limit before the sufficiency direction can be accepted as checked. The PDF text layer garbled several formulas, so some readings are inferred.
strengths: The necessity argument (Sections 2-3) is short and checkable. The Lemma 2 angular identity p'/(2Np) = Im h(e^(2i theta)) was confirmed numerically. f_c with zeta=(c+i)/s gives f'(0)=2ic/s and F+HG=c to 1e-12 at radius 0.9.
The minimization min over c>0 of (a+c)sqrt(1+c^2)/c equals (1+a^(2/3))^(3/2), with minimizer c=a^(1/3). Confirmed numerically for a = 0.1, 0.5, 1, 2 and 8.
The factor Q(x,y) has eigenvalues (1-|zeta|)^2 and (1+|zeta|)^2, so the product of the Q_j is positive definite. Checked by hand.

For Section 7, the Lyapunov function H = r^2 exp(-(b/k) sin 2k theta) satisfies L_f H = -2a r^(2k) H, checked by hand. This supports the stated global asymptotic stability of the single-harmonic family.
Limitations are stated candidly: no minimum-degree rate, no certified quantile selection, and no solver-based proof of feasibility.
weaknesses: Lemma 3 (boundary pair, eqs. 10-13) is central to sufficiency, but its q_c and h_c formulas are not legible in the text layer. I could not check its boundary sign claims.

Eq. (14) sets c = b^(2/3)-1. Lemma 3 requires a0 = c^3 and b0 = s^3 = (1+c^2)^(3/2), which forces c = (b^(2/3)-1)^(1/2). This is probably a lost radical, but as printed the construction does not match its lemma.
The eps->1 limit in Section 3 is asserted. Near the boundary pole of M_c, f has a |.|^(-1/2) singularity, so dominated convergence should be written out.
Proposition 4's displayed error chain ends in 4/N^2. The stated argument gives 2*pi*L/N with L = 2/(1-rho)^2, since the sum of |I_j| is 2*pi and mu(I_j) = 1/N.

Equality exclusion is attributed to the positive minimum of u. Nonnegativity of u with F, G > 0 and mean(u) = 1 already suffices: a zero integral forces w = 0 and then u = 0, contradicting mean(u) = 1.
Corollary 6's necessity for k-harmonics is asserted in a few lines. The reduction from theta to phi = 2 theta with cos(k phi) is plausible but not written out.
Priority and attribution: arXiv:2607.16171 was found by search, but its snippet describes a different cubic field, so attribution of family (1) to Liu and Fitzsimmons is unverified by me.
potential_errors: Eq. (14), c = b^(2/3)-1, is inconsistent with the Lemma 3 requirement c = (b^(2/3)-1)^(1/2) for a0 = c^3 and b0 = s^3. If read literally, the sufficiency construction for b > 1 does not match its lemma.
Proposition 4 error term: the displayed 4/N^2 is inconsistent with the quantile argument, which yields O(1/N). The explicit N bound and the abstract's O(eps^-3) degree claim need rechecking.
Section 7 header parameter (angular speed) appears as '= 0' in the text layer, which would make theta' vanish. It is probably omega != 0; check the source.
strong_novelty_candidates: The exact threshold |b|^(2/3) < 1 + a^(2/3) as the sharp certificate region of the Liu-Fitzsimmons cubic family, with equality excluded even for weak certificates (Theorem 1). It rests on the harmonic pairing of Section 3, whose key steps I checked.

Corollary 6: the same threshold with angular speed omega for single-harmonic families r' = r^(2k+1)(-a + b cos 2k theta), theta' = omega r^(2k), for every k >= 1. The structure checks out, but the necessity argument is less detailed.
